Routing.//: Every module serves /api/v1/{module}. The mobile client's base URL is https://api.diaspora.app/v1, so it addresses /v1/{module}. EnablePrefixCompatibility rewrites the second onto the first before routing, for every module identically. Set it to false on a deployment whose ingress already rewrites; the canonical prefix is then the only one served. Watch diaspora.api.compatibility_rewrites to find out whether anything still uses the alias.

Notifications.//: The Communication Platform. Every value here has a working default in code; the section exists so a deployment can see what it may change without reading the source.

Realtime.//InstanceCount: How many copies of this application the deployment runs. Nothing can detect this at runtime, and a value above 1 with no backplane means live delivery reaches only the members attached to each instance — so the host refuses to start on that combination rather than failing silently, one member at a time.
Realtime.//EnableDetailedErrors: Off outside local development: a hub exception message can carry an identifier or a member's own data, and it reaches a device the platform does not control.

Backplane.//: What carries fan-out between instances. 'None' is single-instance and is the shipped position. Any other value declares that an adapter has been installed beneath the hub; that adapter reads its own connection settings, and no credential for it belongs in this file.

Push.//: The push transport. 'None' ships: the whole delivery path runs and the attempt is recorded as unsupported, so acquiring a provider is a registration rather than a rewrite. 'Loopback' reports success without sending, for local development only — the host refuses it outside Development and Testing.
Push.//credentials: No credential is committed here and none should be. CredentialsPath points at a secret the orchestrator mounts; CredentialsJson exists for a platform with no filesystem to mount into and must arrive from a secret store. Setting both is a startup error, because the one actually used then depends on which the adapter reads first.
Push.//Settings: Free key/value pairs an adapter reads and this module never does. A Firebase Cloud Messaging adapter, for example, is configured entirely by Provider='Firebase', ProjectId, CredentialsPath and any keys it documents here — no vendor name appears anywhere in the platform's own code.

Notifications.//UnsubscribeSigningKey: B13.3. Signs the one-category unsubscribe token in an email footer, which is redeemed with no session behind it. Empty means a key is generated at startup: links then stop working on restart and are refused by any other instance, so a deployment that sends email must supply one from its secret store. It is not a credential for anybody else's service — a leaked one lets somebody unsubscribe any member from any category, which is a denial of notifications rather than a disclosure.
Notifications.//UnsubscribeLinkLifetimeDays: Ninety days. The member this link exists for is the one who has stopped opening the app, so a link that expired in a week would be dead in exactly the mailbox it was meant for.

ForwardedHeaders.//: KnownProxies must list the load balancer / ingress addresses in each deployed environment. Empty here means forwarded headers are ignored, which is the safe default: better to see the proxy address than to trust a spoofable X-Forwarded-For from an unknown source.
